solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unhappily married to office? I don't believe you!

indicators.note: unhappily signals the letters are in a sorry, disordered state and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a claim that a person is miserably wedded to their job.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal retort of disbelief, telling a speaker to stop pretending.

clue.text: Nose must be cold on top of K2

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
taken as written

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter, so only its initial is used

explanation.surface: A climber on the world's second highest peak worries about frostbite on the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Conk is British slang for the nose.

clue.text: Sailor with broken arm, almost completely inert

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters are reassembled in another order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: almost means the word falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A seaman with a fractured limb lies nearly motionless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' turns ARM into MAR; 'almost completely' trims INERT to INER.
explanation.definitionFit: A mariner is a seaman, a synonym for sailor.

clue.text: Cockney hero heading north, finding gold-bearing rock?

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading the letters upwards, back to front

parts.note: a Cockney drops the H, saying hero as 'ERO; the letters also sitting backwards in the printed word is a coincidence, as the H-dropping is the device

explanation.surface: A London champion travels north and strikes gold in the rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, drop initial H; 'heading north' reverses 'ERO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ore is rock from which metal is extracted; the query marks gold as just one example.

clue.text: Brief affair entertaining you at first

indicators.note: to entertain is to host, so one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: a fling is a short-lived love affair

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A short romance that began by charming you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like an adjective for the affair, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A flying visit is a hasty one, so flying can mean brief or short.

clue.text: Stop old flame fleeing from Dalek's cry

indicators.note: fleeing means one part runs off out of the longer word

parts.note: the Daleks of Doctor Who famously shriek 'Exterminate!'
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: A former lover runs away from a screeching Doctor Who villain, hoping to end the danger.
explanation.walkthrough: Daleks are robot villains in the British TV series Doctor Who.
explanation.definitionFit: To terminate something is to end or halt it, a synonym for stop.

clue.text: Judge a little more fair-mindedly?

indicators.note: only a small part of the words that follow is wanted, a run of letters within them

explanation.surface: Should a referee act a touch more even-handedly?
explanation.definitionFit: A ref, short for referee, judges play in a sporting contest.

clue.text: Get some sunshine, did you say?

indicators.note: the query asks about speech, so the word heard is wanted, not the one spelt

parts.note: rays are beams of sunshine

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether a friend suggested they go and sunbathe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get' here means collect, as in getting money together.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise funds is to obtain or collect them, so raise can mean get.

clue.text: More dull praise?

definitions.meaning: the comparative of flat, meaning duller or more lifeless

explanation.surface: Is an even more boring compliment still worth giving?
explanation.definitionFit: Flat means dull, so flatter is more dull; flattering someone is praising them excessively.

clue.text: Look after extremely rowdy room of children

parts.note: to nurse is to care for or look after

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, first and last letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to supervise a very noisy room full of kids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' looks like it intensifies 'rowdy', but it takes RY, the word's ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery is a room set aside for young children to play or sleep.

clue.text: Educated woman eating a yoghurt dish

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside, so one word holds the other

parts.note: Rita is the heroine of the play and film Educating Rita

explanation.surface: A cultured woman tucks into a yoghurt dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Educating Rita is Willy Russell's play about a hairdresser who studies literature.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is an Indian side dish of yoghurt with cucumber or herbs.

clue.text: Being stubborn, I ring tenants anyhow

indicators.note: anyhow means haphazardly, so the letters are jumbled any old way

explanation.surface: An obstinate landlord makes calls to tenants in a careless fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Intransigent means refusing to compromise, a close synonym of obstinate.

clue.text: Bright idea, heading off in downpour?

indicators.note: heading off means the head, or first letter, is removed

parts.note: in British usage a brainstorm can be a sudden clever idea

explanation.surface: A clever thought strikes someone as they set off into heavy rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainstorm is a heavy fall of rain, a synonym of downpour.

clue.text: Type that is needed for a raid

parts.note: a sort is a kind or type
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A commander says what kind of person a raid calls for.
explanation.definitionFit: A sortie is a sudden attack or sally out by troops, a kind of raid.

clue.text: Lure Penny into bad man's embrace

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside another
an embrace holds something within, so the outer word wraps round the letter

parts.note: a sinner is a wrongdoer, a bad man

explanation.surface: A woman named Penny is enticed into a villain's arms.
explanation.walkthrough: Penny looks like a name; it is P.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinner is a revolving fishing lure that attracts fish.

clue.text: Spots Her Majesty having a bit of bacon

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen breaks out in spots while eating bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasher is a single thin slice of bacon.

clue.text: Most pious host concealing an untruth

indicators.note: concealing means hiding something within, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: taken as written
a lie is an untruth

explanation.surface: The most devout person hosting the event is hiding a falsehood.
explanation.definitionFit: Holiest is the superlative of holy, meaning most devout or saintly.

clue.text: Some bits left? My goodness!

definitions.meaning: small fragments left behind, for instance after eating
a mild British exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone surveys the leftovers and exclaims in surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Crumbs are leftover morsels of food, and also a mild interjection of dismay or surprise.

clue.text: City lenders I upset in tactless manner

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: I annoyed bankers in the financial district by speaking without diplomacy.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting indiscreetly means behaving without discretion or tact.

clue.text: Gold coin, second of many found in Channel

indicators.note: found in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a duct is a channel or tube carrying fluid

indicators.note: second of points to the word's second letter alone

explanation.surface: A gold coin, one of many, is discovered in the sea between England and France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' suggests the English Channel but is just a duct.
explanation.definitionFit: A ducat was a gold coin once used across Europe, notably in Venice.

clue.text: Chap repeatedly making you laugh

indicators.note: repeatedly means the piece is given more than once, here twice

parts.note: a chap is a man, he

explanation.surface: A man who keeps on amusing you.
explanation.definitionFit: He-he is a giggle sound, the noise of amusement someone makes when tickled.

clue.text: Something to eat in Barcelona — chorizo?

indicators.note: in says the answer is found inside these words, spanning the two

explanation.surface: A diner in Spain wonders whether a spicy sausage is the snack on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is a tortilla chip, a snack food.

clue.text: Husband grabbing revolutionary's weapon

indicators.note: grabbing means seizing and holding inside, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: a mate is a spouse or partner, here a husband
Che Guevara is the classic revolutionary

explanation.surface: A husband seizes a rebel's weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: Husband looks like H, but it is MATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad heavy blade, used as a tool or weapon.

clue.text: Pass oddly neglected school

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are ignored, keeping the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A school gets through its inspection despite odd neglect.
explanation.definitionFit: A col is a mountain pass, the low point of a ridge between peaks.

clue.text: Turn back briefly, getting stuck in this?

indicators.note: turned back means read from the end, letters reversed
briefly means shortened, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A driver reverses quickly, afraid of becoming bogged down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' shortens TURN to TUR; 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rut is a deep groove where wheels stick, and a routine one gets stuck in.

clue.text: A regular at Christmas giving you permission for a kiss?

definitions.text: A regular at Christmas giving you permission for a kiss?

parts.words: A regular at Christmas giving you permission for a kiss?
parts.note: a seasonal plant hung each December under which kissing is allowed by custom

explanation.walkthrough: Tradition says anyone standing under this hanging sprig may be kissed.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistletoe appears every Christmas, and custom permits a kiss beneath it.
